You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Nozzle: 0.4 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA (high-speed PLA, black)
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm
- Supports: none. Every part has to print without them.

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- print_test(params, parts): optional. If you need to know whether something is going to work but you're not sure, ask the person to print a test of it before you hand in the final design, so you both save time and filament. They print it and tell you how each piece came out.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 12 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.

The counterbore starts at the bed, so the roof is a 16.5 mm bridge, which should be fine under 50 mm, but the hole in the roof looks partly closed and I'm checking whether the circular bridge is causing that.

I'm weighing whether to flip the coupon so the counterbore opens upward, which would remove the 16.5 mm roof bridge entirely. The dovetail's 45° bevel should print without supports in that orientation, and the camera face would end up smooth on the bed, so that looks like the better fix.

I can't get more detail, so I'll design around standard Arca-style assumptions and flag that in the notes. For a safe fit, the clamp's movable jaw is tightened by a knob, so a ±1 mm width tolerance should be fine. I'm weighing a 38 mm nominal width with a 0.2 mm clearance, exposed as a parameter.

I'm settling the dovetail dimensions next: a 3.5 mm bevel with a 10 mm plate thickness, since the lower section is the only part that seats in the clamp and the floor should be fine.

I'm working out the side geometry of the dovetail. A full 45° bevel over a taller section would give more tolerance against the clamp depth, since the lip can contact anywhere along the slope and wedge in. I'm considering a 6 mm bevel with a 10 mm plate thickness, which would leave the top width at 26 mm.

I'm working out the profile in print orientation, with the camera face at z=0 and the wide clamp face at the top, so the 45° bevel overhangs cleanly on the print bed.

I'm sizing the bolt slot and counterbore next: a 20 mm slot along the roughly 60 mm plate, with a 16.5 mm stadium counterbore cut from the wide clamp face to leave a 4.7 mm floor. That puts the bolt head 5.3 mm proud of the camera face, which should suit most sockets, though I'm not sure of the socket depth, so I'll note it and maybe shorten the bolt to 10 mm.

I'm checking the slot and counterbore clearances now: the stadium ends sit at ±6 mm, and at the counterbore depth the plate's half-width is still about 13.7 mm, well clear of the 8.25 mm radius.

I'm weighing the bolt next: the salvaged bolt is the real hardware, since printing a 1/4-20 screw in PLA would be too weak, and its head can sit in the counterbore with the shank running down through the slot.

I'm defining the bolt seat, slot clearance, and camera socket as features, then listing the salvaged bolt as hardware with its measured head and length. I'm also weighing criteria checks for the bolt slot, head seat, and dovetail engagement, and whether to include a small dovetail coupon as a test part.

reasoning_details.text:
I can't get more detail, so I'll design around standard Arca-style assumptions and flag that in the notes. For a safe fit, the clamp's movable jaw is tightened by a knob, so a ±1 mm width tolerance should be fine. I'm weighing a 38 mm nominal width with a 0.2 mm clearance, exposed as a parameter.

I'm settling the dovetail dimensions next: a 3.5 mm bevel with a 10 mm plate thickness, since the lower section is the only part that seats in the clamp and the floor should be fine.

I'm working out the side geometry of the dovetail. A full 45° bevel over a taller section would give more tolerance against the clamp depth, since the lip can contact anywhere along the slope and wedge in. I'm considering a 6 mm bevel with a 10 mm plate thickness, which would leave the top width at 26 mm.

I'm working out the profile in print orientation, with the camera face at z=0 and the wide clamp face at the top, so the 45° bevel overhangs cleanly on the print bed.

I'm sizing the bolt slot and counterbore next: a 20 mm slot along the roughly 60 mm plate, with a 16.5 mm stadium counterbore cut from the wide clamp face to leave a 4.7 mm floor. That puts the bolt head 5.3 mm proud of the camera face, which should suit most sockets, though I'm not sure of the socket depth, so I'll note it and maybe shorten the bolt to 10 mm.

I'm checking the slot and counterbore clearances now: the stadium ends sit at ±6 mm, and at the counterbore depth the plate's half-width is still about 13.7 mm, well clear of the 8.25 mm radius.

I'm weighing the bolt next: the salvaged bolt is the real hardware, since printing a 1/4-20 screw in PLA would be too weak, and its head can sit in the counterbore with the shank running down through the slot.

I'm defining the bolt seat, slot clearance, and camera socket as features, then listing the salvaged bolt as hardware with its measured head and length. I'm also weighing criteria checks for the bolt slot, head seat, and dovetail engagement, and whether to include a small dovetail coupon as a test part.
